findings.summary: Code is shown before its idea is stated in the self-invocation section.
findings.fix: Put the one-line idea (a call to this.get() skips the proxy) directly above the snippet, and keep the conclusion line below it.

findings.summary: The line 'null results are never cached' reads as a general rule, but Spring caches null values by default.
findings.evidence:
@Cacheable(value="products", key="#id", unless="#result==null")
null results are never cached
findings.fix: Reword to: 'unless="#result==null" stops null from being stored. Without it, Spring caches null by default (for example Caffeine allowNullValues=true).'

findings.summary: The outline point that @CachePut must not be mixed with @Cacheable on the same method is only named, with no instruction or reason.
findings.evidence: "Mixing @CachePut and @Cacheable on one method" appears as a bare line under the annotations table.
findings.fix: Rewrite the line as "Do not put @CachePut and @Cacheable on the same method: @Cacheable skips the body on a hit while @CachePut forces it to run, so the two conflict."

findings.summary: A bullet is left incomplete and does not say what happens when @CachePut and @Cacheable are mixed on one method.
findings.fix: Complete it, e.g. 'Do not mix @CachePut and @Cacheable on one method: @Cacheable may skip the body while @CachePut forces it to run.'

findings.summary: The 'Default key' bullet and the SpEL override are two ideas in a short bullet group, and the 'null results are never cached' bullet contradicts the 'unless' example, which implies null caching is configurable.
findings.evidence: unless="#result==null" ... null results are never cached
findings.fix: State plainly that null is cached by default and unless="#result==null" prevents it, or drop the unconditional claim.

findings.summary: The Redis serializer bullet and the per-cache TTL bullet are separate ideas, and the two property sets are shown together without labels, so a learner could read them as one configuration.
findings.evidence: spring.cache.type=caffeine ... spring.cache.type=redis ... use one type at a time
findings.fix: Show the two property blocks as separate labelled snippets (Caffeine / Redis) and put the one-line idea before each.

findings.summary: The default executor sizing is given inaccurately and unexplained.
findings.fix: Say core 8, max Integer.MAX_VALUE, queue capacity unbounded, so page 5 and page 7 on 'max is ignored' follow from it.

findings.summary: The @Async bullet carries several ideas (public, returns immediately, runs on an executor thread, allowed return types).
findings.evidence: On a public bean method: returns immediately, body runs on an executor thread
findings.fix: Split it into one bullet for behaviour and one for the allowed return types.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "surprises", "timezone").
findings.evidence: cron has six fields (second minute hour day month weekday): "0 0 2 * * *" runs daily at 02:00; add zone = "Asia/Kolkata" to avoid server-timezone surprises
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The cron snippet comes before any statement of the idea, and the field order is given as text only.
findings.evidence:
@Scheduled(cron = "0 0 2 * * *", zone = "Asia/Kolkata")
second minute hour day month weekday
findings.fix: Add a short line stating that cron has 6 fields, then show them as a small table or aligned fields above the example.

findings.summary: The scheduling answer is ambiguous and the fixedDelay figure is unsupported.
findings.evidence: Every ~8s, right when the previous run ends ... fixedDelay=5000 would give 13s gaps
findings.fix: Add the reasoning: the run takes 8s, so each late start fires immediately after the previous one ends. Show the 8+5 arithmetic for the 13s gap.
